newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MP quits, coalition majority cut to one seat.
newsitem.headline: Turk MP quits, coalition majority cut to one seat.

text.p: A fourth MP from the secularist wing of Turkey's Islamist-led government has resigned, leaving Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition with a paper majority of only one seat in the 550-seat parliament.
Cefi Kamhi, an MP from Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party, late on Saturday became the fourth MP to resign from the party in recent days, Anatolian news agency said on Sunday.
Anatolian gave no details of why Kamhi, a leading businessman, resigned his seat.
The government coalition has four more MPs than the combined opposition parties since two seats in parliament are vacant.
Erbakan's governemt narrowly survived a censure motion in parliament last week with the help of seven members of a far right-wing Islamist party.

Three ministers from Ciller's secularist party have resigned from the cabinet in protest at what they saw as increased religious zeal on the part of their partners in Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party.
